sc: BEST CUSTOMER
Your best customer keeps making your staff uncomfortable.
BEST CUSTOMER
From the thirtieth of October, that can be on you.
BEST CUSTOMER
Not them. You. If you didn't take all reasonable steps to stop it.
THE LAW
The new law says employers must not permit harassment of their staff by third parties.
That means customers and clients.
THE LAW
A third party is anyone who isn't you or your staff.
Customers, clients, suppliers, contractors.
THE LAW
And it's not just sexual harassment.
It covers harassment linked to things like age, disability, race, religion, sex and sexual orientation.
THE LAW
And your staff can bring a claim against you at an employment tribunal.
4 STEPS
So here's what to do before the thirtieth.
STEP 1
One. Put it in writing.
A harassment policy that covers customers and clients, not just staff.
STEP 2
Two. Make it easy to report.
More than one way to speak up, and act fast when someone does.
STEP 3
Three. Put it in your client contracts and terms.
Set out how your staff must be treated, and what happens if they're not.
STEP 4
Four. Train your team and managers on what to do when it happens.
KEEP TRACK

with a task and an owner for each update. So nothing slips before the deadline.
YOUR TURN
Has a customer ever crossed the line with your team? Yes or no.
